room/perp: A stream of d numbers has room for only d directions at exact right angles. In two dimensions, two features fit perfectly.
room/three: Three features? Give up exact right angles, and spread them a hundred and twenty degrees apart.
room/rows: Each feature's direction is a row of W, an arrow of length one. Feature zero points along one, zero. Features one and two point to minus a half, and plus or minus zero point eight seven.
room/self: Dot a direction with itself, and you get one. For feature zero: one times one, plus zero times zero.
room/pair: Dot two different directions, and you get minus a half: one times minus a half, plus zero times zero point eight seven. Every pair, a hundred and twenty degrees apart, overlaps by that same minus a half.
read/store: Store values by adding up each feature's value times its direction. Say the values, f, are three, zero and two: features zero and two are on.
read/scale: Three times feature zero's direction is three, zero. Two times feature two's is minus one, minus one point seven four.
read/sum: Add them: the stream, x, is two, minus one point seven four. Three values, packed into two numbers.
read/read: Read feature zero back with a dot product: two times one, plus minus one point seven four times zero. Two, not three.
read/split: Why two? The stream is three of feature zero's direction plus two of feature two's, so the dot product splits into pieces: three times one, plus two times minus a half.
read/rule: So a reading is the feature's own value, plus minus a half times each other value that is on. The minus one is the leak, called interference, and it grows with the other feature's value.
sparse/rare: Interference only happens between features that are on at the same time. If each feature is rare, on for one token in a hundred, two at once are rarer still.
sparse/clip: Most of the time one feature is on alone. Its neighbors read small negative leaks, and a ReLU clips them to zero.
sparse/more: In many dimensions, far more than d directions can be nearly perpendicular. So a model can store many more sparse features than it has dimensions. That is superposition.
try/p1: Try one. The same three directions hold the values two, one and three. What does reading feature one give?
try/own: Start from its own value, one. Each other value leaks in at minus a half: minus a half times two is minus one, and minus a half times three is minus one and a half.
try/a1: Add them: one, minus one, minus one and a half. Minus one and a half.
try/p2: Now the values are a half, two and one, and a ReLU follows the reading. Read feature zero.
try/a2: A half, minus one, minus a half: minus one. The ReLU clips it to zero.
